## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dfbf137fa5b615a29a470ca4bf4cf150521e8729`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11196 (body; comments `5909012131`, `5909773493`, `5909998189`, `5914143054`), PR #11224 (body, its 19 files, the three-dot diff against `main`), the head's check-runs with `filter=latest` (polled 15:17Z, 15:25Z and at post time), card #8219 with its 13 comments for ③.1, and `contents` reads at `main` and at the head for context. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The head carries no gate verdict, and cannot: the PR does not merge into `main`.** `dfbf137fa` has 0 check-runs at every poll. The five suites GitHub lists on it (vercel, fly-io, claude, cloudflare-workers-and-pages, objectstack-fleet) are app placeholders, each `queued` with 0 runs; the only commit status is Vercel. The branch has 0 workflow runs at ANY of its heads, where a PR head in this repo normally carries 45 `github-actions` runs (PR #11222's head `573373f93`, for one). The cause is on the PR record: `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: dirty`, `merge_commit_sha: null`. The branch's merge base with `main` is `340dc718f` (13:24Z); `main` is 7 commits past it, and `e6bc087a3` (PR #11207, objectui#11197, 13:42Z) edits three files this PR edits: `AppPreview.tsx`, `AppNavCanvas.tsx` and `NavigationDesigner.tsx`. In `AppPreview.tsx` both sides touch the same import lines (this PR rewrites the `resolveHref` import and inserts after the `resolveI18nLabel` line; `main` inserts `NavigationItemType` between them), so the merge is dirty and a `pull_request` workflow does not run. The two base merges brought only `main`'s own changes: `a0f4a0de1` (second parent `9419df198`, objectui#11206's fix) and `62e7aff21` (second parent `340dc718f`) both merge `main` commits, and the three-dot diff lists exactly the 19 files with only this PR's hunks; but the `main` they merged was fetched before 13:35Z, so PR #11207 is not in the branch. Every derived gate family (Type Check, Lint, the 8 test shards, dist pins, Build and E2E, Changeset Declaration / Bump Policy / Fixed Group / Claim Re-read, Spec Main Shape Gate, Bundle Analysis, README Export Check, Pre-Install Import Graph, Control Byte Scan, Line Citation Gate) is unanswered at this head; the dev's local readings are the only evidence, and this brief makes the check-runs the verdicts. **Wrong, and it decides the verdict.** What clears it: merge `main`, resolve `AppPreview.tsx` (after the merge its `NavKind` is the spec-derived `NavigationItemType`, which has `doc`; the parity pin's `LABEL_LESS` list should gain a `doc` entry, whose runtime arm answers `doc` else `book`), push, let the roster complete, and a record on that head re-judges.

**2. Each surface calls `resolveNavItemLabel`; no ladder is restated.** Read hunk by hunk:
- `AppPreview` list and landing line: `normalizeNav` asks `navEntryLabelText(it, locale, targetLabel)`; the existence test keeps reading the AUTHORED label (`navItemLabelText`, the same `resolveI18nLabel ?? ''` it read before), so inherited text never lists an entry with nothing to open; `label || unnamed` applies only after the rule answered `''`. The landing line derives from the same `navItems` (`→ Leads` pinned). Right.
- `AppNavCanvas` card and inline rename: `navLabel` asks `navEntryLabelText`; the positional `engine.appNav.item` row is reached only on `''` (a separator, an empty map, no target and no `id`). The rename input's state is the AUTHORED text (`navItemLabelText(item.label)`), `placeholder={label}` is the inherited text, blur writes only when `v && v !== authored`, Escape resets to the authored text. An untouched entry writes nothing (pinned). Right.
- `AppNavInspector` title and Label field: `labelOf = navEntryLabelText(...).trim() || selection.id`; the field's `value` is `navItemLabelText(node.label, locale)` and its `placeholder` is `inheritedNavEntryText(node, targetLabel)`; `InspectorTextField` takes `placeholder` (`_shared.tsx`). `commitLabel('')` goes to `clearedLabel`, and `undefined` becomes `patch({}, ['label'])`, which DELETES the key: never `''`. A map loses only the designer locale's own entry (exact tag, else bare language; an entry reached only as a fallback is kept), and a map with no text left clears to no key. `NavItem.title` / `name` are gone from the type and the reads. Right.
- `nav-selection.ts`: `findNavPositionById` returns `label` only for a plain-string authored label; the `title ?? name` rungs are gone. Its two callers select by `hit.selectionId`; `ResourceEditPage.tsx` also forwards `hit.label` into the selection, which for a spec-valid label-less entry was already `undefined` (only an off-spec `title` / `name` document loses that rung), and the inspector now titles the entry from the entry itself. Right.
- Studio rail `NavTree` rows: the group heading and the leaf both read `navEntryLabelText(node, locale, targetLabel)`; the leaf's `|| surface?.name` is reached only on `''`; the tooltip keeps `type · name` (objectui#7254's reachable half; pinned as the accessible description). Right.
- plugin-designer `NavigationDesigner` rows and live preview: `resolveNavItemLabel(item)` itself, and the rename input's placeholder is the same call. For an authored label the answer equals the old `resolveKeyedI18nLabel(item.label)`: a string is itself; a keyed label is `defaultValue || key`; with no resolvers `resolveNavItemLabel` returns `base`. So the control is unchanged. Right.
- `AppCreationWizard` Navigation step: `NavigationBuilderStep` builds `targetLabel` from `draft.objects` (name → `label`) and hands it as the rule's sixth argument; it answers `object` targets and `undefined` for everything else, leaving the ladder to the rule. That is a `NavTargetLabelResolver` implementation, the host's answer to "what is this target called", not a second resolver. Right.
- Ladder census on label-less paths: `|| unnamed` (AppPreview), `tFormat('engine.appNav.item')` (canvas), `|| selection.id` (inspector), `|| surface?.name` (rail) each apply only after the rule answered `''`. No `label ?? title ?? name ?? id` remains. Right.

**3. `useNavTargetLabel` over a designer-locale twin.** Measured right: `useMetadataLocale()` is `/^zh/i.test(language) ? 'zh-CN' : 'en-US'` over the same `useObjectTranslation().language` the hook resolves in, and the hook is memoised on `[metadata, objectLabel, viewLabel, dashboardLabel, language]`, so the `useMemo` in `AppPreview` holds. The direction's first option names exactly this (`resolveNavItemLabel` with the shared `useNavTargetLabel`). The residual for the eight other locales is acceptable and disclosed: the designer already draws its chrome and authored map labels in `en-US` for those sessions, so the language mix predates this PR, and the inherited text is by construction what the console draws, which is the parity the card asks for. A twin later is a one-argument swap at each call site; it does not change this PR's shape. Right.

**4. `navItemLabel.ts` extended, not forked.** `inheritedNavEntryText` calls `resolveNavItemLabel({ ...entry, label: undefined }, undefined ×4, targetLabel)`; the `typeof text === 'string' ? text : ''` guard covers a loosely typed draft with no `id` (the runtime's last rung is `item.id`). `navEntryLabelText` keys on `entry.label !== undefined`, as the runtime keys on `item.label === undefined`; a present-but-empty map answers `''` and is not treated as absent, matching the runtime's arm. `clearedLabel` is `renamedLabel`'s inverse through the shared `ownEntryKey`; `renamedLabel` keeps its `?? locale.trim()` fallback, so its behaviour is unchanged. The docblock carries the carrier rider (`5909012131`): `navItemLabelText` reads any `I18nLabel`; the rename was rightly left, since it would touch `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` and `ObjectActionsPanel.tsx`. The module is not exported from the package root (`packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` exports the metadata-admin pages only). Right.

**5. plugin-designer's `@object-ui/layout` dependency.** `dependencies`, `workspace:*`; the lock gains only the importer link. Layout depends on components, core, react, types, spec, dnd-kit and lucide; none reaches plugin-designer. Cycle-free, not inlined (the dev's measured 1 external import / 0 inlined ladders is consistent with a vite build that externalises bare specifiers). Right; the level is judged in ②.

**6. `engine.appPreview.unnamed` and `engine.appNav.item`** now cover only what the rule names nothing (a separator, an empty map, no target and no `id`); the three re-judged pins (`AppPreview.labelMaps-11100`, `AppNavCanvas.labelMaps-11128`, `AppPreview.test.tsx`) say so and keep the fallbacks for those cases. No hunk touches `i18n.ts`; no key added or removed. Right.

**7. Ablations.** A to D at `2a6f0c5fb` (app-shell source unchanged after it; `NavigationDesigner.tsx` unchanged after it), E at `dfbf137fa` (1 of 4 red on `Contact`), the void E at `d78e28afd` correctly discarded. Each leg mutates the surface its pin covers. Right in shape, but every reading is the dev's own: with finding 1 no gate has confirmed a single pin green on this head.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `11196-designer-nav-label-inherit.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`, `@object-ui/plugin-designer: patch`. No exported surface moves: `navItemLabel.ts`, `nav-selection.ts`, the inspector and the previews are not root exports of app-shell (they reach the registry through `register-builtins.js`, unchanged); `NavigationDesignerProps` and `AppCreationWizardProps` are unchanged, the wizard's new `objects` prop sits on the internal `NavigationBuilderStep`, and the rename input gains DOM attributes only. The new package-graph edge (plugin-designer → layout, a fixed-group sibling of the 39) is disclosed in the changeset's last line; the repo's policy forbids only `major` (AGENTS.md: the fixed group publishes together; `check-changeset-presence` deliberately leaves `dependencies` unguarded), so `patch` is admissible. Noted for the seat, not a finding: `@object-ui/layout` is `sideEffects`-true, so a host that imports plugin-designer without layout now also runs layout's registry registrations; the console already ships layout. **`Clause-②: no` — right:** no schema, prop, type or accepted set moves, stored nav documents are unchanged, and the PR body carries the line.

**One defect in the changeset text (in the diff, and it ships in the CHANGELOG):** its lines 27 to 29, "The Navigation Designer and the wizard are handed bare items and no metadata, so they show the rule's machine-name rung (`pageName`, `dashboardName`, `objectName`, …), which is what the console shows for a page." Since `d78e28afd` the wizard's Navigation step hands the rule a resolver built from its own object list, and a label-less object entry shows the object's label (pinned: `Contact`). The sentence is false for the wizard. The dev's deviation flagged the PR body only; the changeset carries the same sentence and must say that NavigationDesigner shows the machine-name rung while the wizard's Navigation step inherits each object's label from the wizard's object list. Wrong.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`navSurface.ts` `resolveSurface` listed in the claim, left unchanged (open question 1).** Reading of objectui#8219 item 3, from its thread: the RULING is seat answer `5837066449` applying objectui#7254 — the chip reads the item's LABEL, and `type · name` stays reachable on the tooltip. The `type · name` TEXT for an unlabelled leaf is the pre-existing fallback that `StudioDesignSurface.aiChipLabel.test.tsx` records ("an unlabelled leaf: the chip falls back to type · name"), and the 8219 seat declined to change the unlabelled-leaf fallback because it would revisit #7254 (`5836130195`, item 4: "not a seat call"). Since then triage `5909773493` ruled for THIS card, above seat level, that every designer surface resolves an absent label through the runtime's rule, and the card's SEAM list names `navSurface.ts (resolveSurface)`. So item 3 is a pin, and the unlabelled-leaf question is already re-ruled for the designer surfaces. Reading: **A** — `resolveSurface` takes an optional `NavTargetLabelResolver`, its callers in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` (`NavTree`, the load effect's first-leaf pick, the `?surface=` restore) pass `useNavTargetLabel`, and the aiChipLabel unlabelled-leaf case is re-pinned to the inherited text with `type · name` on the title, which keeps #7254's reachable half. Note for that re-pin: it clicks the rail row by the name `b2r4_customer 对象`, which under this PR is the inherited label whenever metadata labels the object; the pin has no `MetadataProvider`, so it still resolves to the machine name today. The dev was right to stop: the callers are outside "`NavTree` rows only". Serial after PR #11225, which edits `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`.
2. **`StudioNavItemInspector` (open question 2).** Reading: **A**, after PR #11225 lands (it edits `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` and `AppCreationWizard.tsx`, both also edited here; whichever lands second merges `main`). Its `''` write through `renamedLabel`, its missing placeholder and its bind storing the object's label are the same defect class this PR fixes in `AppNavInspector`, with the same module functions (`clearedLabel`, `inheritedNavEntryText`); two editors of one label must agree, which is `navItemLabel.ts`'s stated purpose. Not a new card.
3. **`addItem`'s "New item" birth label (open question 3).** Reading: **A** as a follow-up after PR #11225, seat-level: a stored birth sentinel is exactly what inheritance replaces; B is sentinel matching, which the runtime arm refuses for a label spelled like a machine name; the #11189 autosave pins that count `New item` saves are the seat's to re-rule. Rightly not done here.
4. **`NavigationDesigner` with no metadata (open question 4).** Reading: **A** (leave). The direction accepts the rule's own answer for a host that supplies no resolver, and no producer in the repo renders `navigation-designer` with app metadata. B is a published prop (`Clause-②: yes`) for a card of its own when a host appears.
5. **The PR body is false at this head** (objectui squash-merges with it). The false sentences, exactly:
   - "This designer is handed bare items and no metadata, so it shows the rule's machine-name rung." (the plugin-designer bullet, read for the package's two surfaces: false for the wizard step; the two sentences after it hold for NavigationDesigner only);
   - "The only later commit, `693024cc2`, edits the changeset alone; the gates that read it were re-run there (last group below)." (`d78e28afd` and `dfbf137fa` follow it and edit plugin-designer source and its pin);
   - "objectui#11197 holds `NavigationRenderer.tsx` and edits `NavigationDesigner.tsx`'s pin-lag type key; this PR edits only that file's label reads. The two regions are disjoint." (PR #11207 also edited `AppPreview.tsx` and `AppNavCanvas.tsx`, and the branch now conflicts with `main`, ①.1);
   - "Known external red: none expected." (there is no CI on this head at all).
   Table row 7 ("`AppCreationWizard`'s Navigation step … the rule's own answer") is not false but should split the wizard (inherits each object's label from the wizard's own list). Ablation E belongs in the ablation list (1 of 4 red at `dfbf137fa`, the `Contact` assertion), and the plugin-designer re-measure at `dfbf137fa` (28 files / 203 tests, type-check 0) belongs in the Tests section. The changeset fix is ② above.
6. **The 43-minute lock hold.** The fixed double is stable in the code: `client` is a `vi.hoisted` singleton returned by the `useMetadataClient` mock; `useMetadataOptions`'s effect deps are `[client, type, rowFilter]`, where `type` is a constant per nav type and `rowFilter` is the module-level `isStaticPageOption` or `undefined`; the `MetadataCtx` value is a module-level constant, so `useNavTargetLabel`'s memo is stable too. The render settles. Confirmed.
7. **`ensureNavId` `nav_object_object` (carrier: none).** Confirmed in `inspectors/nav-target.ts`: with no `id`, no `objectName`, a map label and no seed, `String(node.label)` is `[object Object]`, which slugs to `object_object`. Pre-existing and untouched here; the spec requires an `id`; a p3 card or a carrier note is the seat's call. Not a finding against this PR.
8. Also answered: `Part of #11196`, not `Fixes` — right, two SEAM sites remain (③.1, ③.2). `plugin-designer/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` outside the claim's list — right, the claim's direction (call `resolveNavItemLabel` from plugin-designer) implies the dependency, and the lock gains only the link. Commit `7906f5f19`'s prose "Part of objectui#11196." — the squash uses the PR body; no trailer; nothing to do. The serial note for the seat: PR #11225 and this PR both edit `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` and `AppCreationWizard.tsx`.

**Findings that decide the verdict:** (1) no gate ran on `dfbf137fa` because the PR conflicts with `main` (①.1); (2) the changeset's wizard sentence is false at this head (②). Everything else judged above is right.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-11196-designer-nav-label-inherit`
Reviewed-by: `session_011p7ikEivgXefNDaE5S5Uec`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Moving the family with it in `pnpm-lock.yaml` collapses the duplicate; every declared range already admitted 17.3.0, so no manifest moved.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.
